system: You are the lead AI reviewer on a deal team. Read the following PRIMARY due-diligence documents and write a concise summary for the partner: key findings, red flags, and a recommendation. Connect issues across documents where relevant.

exchanges.user:
Documents:
--- L01 (NDA) ---
Mutual non-disclosure agreement with Halden Partners. Two-year term. Standard carve-outs. No non-solicitation clause.

--- L02 (Lease) ---
Head office lease, Level 3, 41 Coolidge Street. Five-year term from 2024, market rent review in year three. Landlord consent needed for assignment; clause 19 says a change of control is not an assignment.

--- L03 (Management accounts - revenue) ---
FY revenue AUD 18.4m, up 9%. Gross margin 61%. Largest customer Arlen Health, 41% of revenue; next largest customer 7%.

--- L04 (HR) ---
Headcount 94. Standard employment contracts. Twelve-month retention letters signed by the CTO and the Head of Sales.

--- L05 (Customer contract) ---
Master services agreement with Arlen Health, renewed 1 July 2025 for five years. Services: platform licence, hosting and support. Fees: annual, CPI-indexed, invoiced quarterly in advance. Service levels: 99.9% monthly uptime; service credits capped at 10% of monthly fees. Data: customer data hosted in Australia; ISO 27001 certification maintained. Liability: capped at twelve months' fees, except data breach (three times annual fees). Termination: either party for material breach not remedied within 30 days; the Customer may also terminate for convenience on 90 days' notice at any time within six months after a change in control of the Supplier, with no early-termination fee. Governing law: New South Wales. Notices: by email to nominated contacts.

--- L06 (Bank facility) ---
AUD 6m revolving facility with Southgate Bank, expiring 2027. Leverage covenant: net debt to EBITDA not more than 2.5x, tested quarterly.

--- L07 (Email) ---
Email from the CFO, M. Iredale, to the Chair, 14 April: 'To be clear for the board pack: we breached the leverage covenant at the 31 March test date, 2.9x against the 2.5x limit. The bank has not been notified yet. I will raise it with them after the board meeting.'

--- L08 (Internal note) ---
Note from the Head of Customer Success, T. Okafor: 'I can't be sure, but the uptick in small-business churn this quarter might be linked to the January price change. It's too early to say, and the numbers are small.'

--- L09 (Insurance) ---
Professional indemnity and cyber cover to AUD 10m, renewed in March. No notified claims.

--- L10 (IP) ---
Platform code written by employees under standard IP assignment clauses. Two open-source components, under MIT and Apache 2.0 licences.

--- L11 (Supplier) ---
Hosting with a major cloud provider on standard online terms. Monthly billing, no minimum commitment.

--- L12 (Board minutes) ---
Board meeting, 20 March. Approved the FY budget and hiring plan. Noted a strong sales pipeline. No other business.

--- L13 (Policy) ---
Privacy policy updated for the 2025 amendments. Annual staff privacy training completed.

--- L14 (Vendor contract) ---
Office cleaning contract, twelve months, terminable on 30 days' notice.

--- L15 (Fixed assets) ---
Laptops and office fit-out. Written-down value AUD 0.4m.

Write the DD summary now.
exchanges.text:
## Partner DD summary

**Recommendation: proceed only subject to resolving the bank covenant breach and protecting against Arlen Health’s post-acquisition termination right.** These are material financing and revenue risks; headline growth does not offset them.

### Key findings and red flags

- **Bank covenant breach—urgent.** The CFO confirms leverage of **2.9x versus a 2.5x limit** at 31 March and states that the bank had not been notified as of the 14 April email (L06–L07). Current notification and waiver status are unknown. Obtain the full facility terms, assess default consequences and secure a written waiver and any required transaction consent before completion. Delayed notification also raises governance concerns.

- **Customer concentration compounded by change-of-control risk.** Arlen contributes **41% of revenue—approximately AUD 7.5m annually** (L03). Despite its five-year renewal, Arlen may terminate without an early-termination fee on 90 days’ notice exercised within six months after supplier change of control (L05). Losing this revenue could materially impair earnings and worsen the existing leverage problem. Seek a binding waiver of this right and validate the relationship directly; reflect unresolved exposure in valuation and deal protection.

- **Positive trading, but earnings resilience needs testing.** Revenue is AUD 18.4m, up 9%, with 61% gross margin (L03). The possible link between January price increases and small-business churn is explicitly tentative, with small numbers—not an established trend (L08). Validate churn, retention and customer-level profitability, and stress-test liquidity and covenant headroom under customer-loss scenarios.

- **Data obligations create meaningful exposure.** Arlen requires Australian data hosting, maintained ISO 27001 certification and 99.9% monthly uptime; data-breach liability is capped at three times annual fees (L05). If Arlen’s reported revenue approximates annual contractual fees, that is roughly **AUD 22.6m**, exceeding the stated AUD 10m insurance cover (L09). Verify the fee basis, compliance, policy limits and exclusions. Privacy training and an updated policy do not establish operational compliance (L13).

### Other findings

- CTO and Head of Sales have signed 12-month retention letters; confirm commencement, enforceability and post-close coverage (L04).
- Employee IP assignments and permissively licensed open-source components are reassuring, subject to ownership and licence-compliance verification (L10).
- The office lease expressly excludes change of control from assignment, reducing that consent risk; a year-three market rent review remains a cost uncertainty (L02).
- Monthly cloud hosting without minimum commitments provides flexibility, but supplier continuity, security and service terms should be checked against Arlen obligations (L11).

**Completion priorities:** bank waiver and financing certainty; Arlen change-of-control waiver; validated downside forecasts; and confirmation of data compliance and insurance adequacy.
